Completeness comes from requiring all expected top-level runtime events and every observed descendant, all intended packages, consistent wrapper/package exits and existing failure/skip controls. A source-derived name that cannot compile/run leads to noncompletion rather than an invented success.

An unexpected runtime top-level identity must reject instead of being ignored. A missed source-derived identity therefore does not license accepting an unknown runtime case. Diagnostic/collision/context inconsistencies also stay unresolved.
